chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: New Year's Eve full dress and Mavouzy's overplaying
summary: Butler put on full dress at intermission; Mavouzy imitated badly, threatened him, then overplayed Cherokee, and Butler brought the crowd up with Night Train.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: So one New Year's Eve, at that time on New Year's Eve I always put my full dress on. So Mavouzy--12:00 o'clock--about quarter to 12, I'm going to bring the New Year in in style. So I put the full dress on at intermission. Mavouzy looked, and they said, "Mavouzy, do you see what he's got on?" Mavouzy said, "I'm going to get mine, too. Don't let him make us feel bad." See, that was (unintelligible) he's in the band. "He wants you to play beguine." And the man said, "I don't want any beguines because you all are buying red wine and these Americans are buying all that heavy whisky, buying these doubles, and I'm overcharging them anyway. Don't you bother. Don't fool with that."

And Mavouzy went home--got a taxi. He lived in Brooklyn--and put his full dress on. Remember... had a great belt on and the shoes he had on (inaudible) got to be careful. And he had the pants that would be sort of robust around the hips and everything. And his collar was way in. And his belt was sticking out through the vest and it stuck out a little bit and the coat was open and the tails come
Just lifted an arm and everything didn't raise up.
And Mavouzy made a gesture with his arm and his whole suit might be on his shoulders?
Yeah, and the belt was showing. And you don't wear no belt with fancy dress.
Well, he wouldn't know about cumberbuns.

(Inaudible). So Mavouzy come in and looked in the mirror, and looked at me. He said, 'I'm going to beat you up.' I said, 'Yes, I was prepared for that.' I said, 'But you going to beat him up (inaudible). He said, 'You got a revolver?' I said, 'Yeah, well, you say you're going to beat me, I said, but you've got to beat him up, too. Mavouzy went downstairs and took a chorus, we're playing 'Cherokee' and Mavouzy playing -- he played about half out (humming). Come on, Mavouzy, go on, go ahead now. (Unintelligible). And I know he's going to play and play and play until (inaudible). Get (inaudible). 'Thank you ladies and

gentlemen, we'll have an intermission now." (Unintelligible). He went back there in the back and sat down. He said, I don't know what happened to me. I said, "Are you coming up again?" So Mavouzy was quiet all night. All night.

Then I went into "Night Train" and started the place to jumping. And Mavouzy come up there and said, "I can't understand what you're doing, because you have these people jumping, stamping their feet." I said, "Well, you follow my lead, you're my boy." And then I said, "You know what happened to you, don't you?" He said, "What?" I said, "Well, you just overplayed yourself and you've got to stop that because you'll have a heart attack man." (Inaudible). He said, "I love you, Jacques, but you want to make a fool out of me in front of my friends."
